advisory_findings.title: Chat 400 error shape includes `details` while sibling routes do not
advisory_findings.description: The chat route returns `{ error: 'Invalid input', details: parsed.error.flatten() }` on Zod failure, while `/api/roleplay-attempts` returns `{ error: 'Missing required fields' }` and `/api/lesson-complete` returns `{ error: 'Invalid input' }` — both without a `details` field. The `details` field is additive and not consumed by the chat-tutor client (which checks `!res.ok` and shows a generic error). This is not a contract violation but creates a minor inconsistency across the sales-advantage API surface.
advisory_findings.evidence: Client code at components/chat-tutor.tsx:46 checks `if (!res.ok || !res.body) throw new Error('chat failed')` — never reads the error body. The `details` field is purely informational for debugging.
advisory_findings.recommendation: Consider standardizing error shapes across all routes, or adopting the `details` pattern everywhere for consistency. No fix required for this phase.

advisory_findings.title: Chat 429 response omits `retryAfter` that roleplay-attempts includes
advisory_findings.description: The chat route's 429 response is `{ error: 'Rate limit exceeded' }` while the roleplay-attempts route returns `{ error: 'Rate limit exceeded', retryAfter: rateLimit.retryAfter }`. The `checkRateLimit` function returns `retryAfter` in both cases, but the chat route discards it. The chat client doesn't use it either (same generic error handler), so no functional impact.
advisory_findings.evidence: route.ts line 41-44 vs roleplay-attempts/route.ts line 32-35. Both call `checkRateLimit()` which returns `{ allowed, retryAfter? }`.
advisory_findings.recommendation: Include `retryAfter` in the chat 429 response for consistency and future client improvements.

advisory_findings.title: Regex strips entire role word + colon, not just the colon
advisory_findings.description: The regex `/(^\|\s)(REP|COACH):/gi` with replacement `$1` removes the entire matched token including the role word. For example, `"REP:sales"` becomes `"sales"` (not `"REPsales"`), and `"Please address me as REP: Sales Coach."` becomes `"Please address me as  Sales Coach."`. This is correct behavior for preventing prompt injection (the word `COACH:` must not appear in user content), but is more aggressive than a colon-only strip. In the sales coaching context, users would not type `REP:` or `COACH:` in their messages, so the practical impact is negligible.
advisory_findings.evidence: Regex test: `"REP:sales".replace(/(^|\s)(REP|COACH):/gi, '$1')` → `"sales"`. The entire `REP:` token is removed. This is intentional and correct for security.
advisory_findings.recommendation: No fix needed — the behavior is correct for prompt injection defense. Document the aggressiveness in the JSDoc if desired.
